subject: AeroThera pilot: request for temporary SLO/latency carveout and commercial terms
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: AeroThera pilot: request for temporary SLO/latency carveout and commercial terms

Team — quick summary and ask. AeroThera (large imaging SaaS prospect) wants to run a three-month production pilot that will be customer-facing. Their procurement/legal are asking for two non-standard items: (1) a temporary reduction in the uptime SLO from our standard 99.99% to 99.95% for the pilot period, and (2) a p95 latency guardrail of 200ms (currently we guarantee p95 < 150ms on dedicated). They are asking for a commercial concession to offset perceived risk: a one-time 15% pilot discount on monthly fees and a capped service-credit exposure tied to the pilot.

Deal context: expected pilot ARR run-rate ~$86k/month, potential enterprise expansion in Q3. Procurement has time pressure — they want a signed amendment by next Wednesday to meet their vendor cutover. Risk/ops: lowering uptime increases customer-facing risk and sets a precedent for other regulated prospects.

Attachments: SLO_carveout_summary.pdf (technical mitigation and rollback plan), Commercial_Memo_AeroThera.docx (pricing ask).

Ask: Ben — can Deal Desk scope acceptable remediation/remedy caps and draft the amendment language? Logan — need finance signoff on the proposed discount and service-credit ceiling. Marissa — can you weigh in for exec signoff (VP) or flag if this should go up to the CRO?

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AeroThera pilot: request for temporary SLO/latency carveout and commercial terms

Chloe — thanks for the quick brief and attaching the memo. I reviewed the technical mitigation doc with Ops. Proposal from Deal Desk:

- Approve temporary uptime SLO of 99.95% limited to the three-month pilot (start date and end date explicit in amendment).
- Approve a latency carveout phrased as "pilot guardrail": p95 <= 200ms; if p95 > 200ms for two consecutive weeks we trigger a remediation plan and a temporary escalation cadence.
- Service credit cap at 5% of monthly pilot fee per month (absolute cap; credits cannot exceed total invoiced pilot fee).
- Commercial concession: 15% pilot discount (first invoice only) or 15% applied pro-rata across the pilot months (open to negotiation).

Conditions:
1) CS must deliver a runbook and on-call rotation for the pilot (attached as an appendix).
2) We include an automatic rollback clause: if latency or availability regressions persist beyond remediation window (14 days), Redwood reserves right to revert to a non-public pilot or suspend the pilot while we remediate — no credits beyond the 5% cap.

I drafted suggested amendment language in Commercial_Memo_AeroThera.docx. My recommendation: approve with VP signoff (Marissa) + Finance thumbs-up (Logan). If ok, I'll prepare a DocuSign amendment and a short internal risk note for Legal.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AeroThera pilot: request for temporary SLO/latency carveout and commercial terms

Thanks Ben — I like the framing. A few leadership conditions before I grant exec approval:

- Timebox the concession to the explicit pilot window and require a dated review meeting between AeroThera, CS, and Product two weeks before pilot end to confirm metrics and go/no-go.
- Reduce the one-time commercial concession to a 10% one-time credit (vs 15%) but allow Chloe the flexibility to apply the 10% across the first invoice or split across months if needed for procurement alignment.
- Add a clause that any future standard contract cannot reference this pilot as precedence for uptime terms — must be explicitly excluded in the amendment.

If Logan confirms finance is comfortable with the 5% monthly credit cap and the one-time 10% concession, I will sign off and ask Legal to fast-track the amendment. Chloe — please confirm AeroThera's desired start date so Legal can pin exact dates.

Marissa Cole
VP, Americas Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AeroThera pilot: request for temporary SLO/latency carveout and commercial terms

Jessica / Daniel — appreciate the quick conversations this week. Internal signoff update: Redwood will approve a timeboxed pilot amendment with the following agreed points: 

- Uptime SLO: temporary 99.95% for the 3-month pilot period.
- Latency guardrail: p95 <= 200ms; remediation plan if two consecutive weeks exceed guardrail.
- Service credit exposure capped at 5% of the monthly pilot fee per month.
- Commercial concession: 10% one-time pilot credit (applied to first invoice unless you prefer pro-rata across pilot months).
- Precedence clause: this amendment will not establish terms for any subsequent standard contract.

Next steps: Ben will send a DocuSign amendment (link below) with the exact pilot window and rollback language. Please confirm desired pilot start date by EOD tomorrow so Legal can finalize dates; we aim to have an executed amendment by Wednesday.
